newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND'S NEW GDANSK YARD SIGNS DEAL FOR 5 SHIPS.
newsitem.headline: POLAND'S NEW GDANSK YARD SIGNS DEAL FOR 5 SHIPS.

text.p: Nowa Stocznia Gdanska Sp. zoo signed a contract with Germany's Schoeller Holding Ltd for the construction of five container ships worth $27.5 million each, the receiver of the bankrupt old Gdansk shipyard said.

Wieslaw Szaj said the contract awarded to a company carved out of the Gdansk shipyard specifies that Scholler would not give any pre-payments to the yard and that the entire construction would be financed by credit given by a consortium led by Bank Gdanski SA.
"The next step in saving the Gdansk shipyard should be the organisation of a consortium led by Bank Gdanski SA to grant credit worth $101.7 million," Szaj told Reuters.
"It will likely be a conditional credit agreement which will depend on whether the state treasury would guarantee the credit," Szaj added.
Szaj said he hoped the consortium would be formed and credit secured by mid-February so that the yard could build the first three 1,500 teu vessels by December 31, 1997.
The remaining two ships were due August 8, 1998, according to the contract.
The old Gdansk shipyard -- where 17 years ago Lech Walesa founded the Solidarity, the first free trade union in the then Soviet bloc -- has operated under bankruptcy rules since August 1996.
Nowa Stocznia Gdanska, carved out of the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard's assets, is not burdened with its parent's debts which exceed 415 million zlotys ($142 million).
